heading: Ablating one attention layer makes later attention layers compensate, restoring much of the output.
definition: ablating one attention layer makes later attention layers compensate, restoring much of the output.
summary: Independent studies support downstream compensation, but use different ablations or qualitative examples and do not quantify restored output. Other tests find no compensation on flat or N-gram data and weak repair in tabular models.

suggested_status.by_scale: toy/synthetic-data models: R0 (only arXiv:2603.06592: weak in the 6-layer hierarchical toy, observed in the 17M PCSG model, absent on flat/N-gram data); <1B: R0 (same study's 17M model; counts versions.V1.studies_by_size '<1B' = 2); 1-10B: R2 (original on Chinchilla 7B; independent arXiv:2603.06592 on OLMo-1B, figure-only; lw:Q8KmWzbituyGCkSro on llama-3-8b, qualitative); 10-100B and >100B: no studies (counts versions.V1.studies_by_size has no such key). Non-language tabular transformers: limited (lw:NpBufh2z2w4mgHKvm, 0–11% repaired).
suggested_status.reason: The original reports layer compensation on Chinchilla 7B (arXiv:2307.15771#R1, arXiv:2307.15771#R3, arXiv:2307.15771#R5). A different author group (counts: versions.V1.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original = 0) reports layerwise Hydra compensation on OLMo-1B and a 17M LLaMA-based PCSG model (arXiv:2603.06592#r3, arXiv:2603.06592#r4, arXiv:2603.06592#r5, arXiv:2603.06592#r6, supports). This study is T2: it zero-ablates whole-layer residual contributions rather than resampling attention sublayers. Its large-model measure is restricted to the immediately following layer's predictive-influence change, its values are figure-only, and it does not quantify restored output. An informal post shows qualitative compensation in llama-3-8b on one arithmetic prompt (lw:Q8KmWzbituyGCkSro#r1, lw:Q8KmWzbituyGCkSro#r2, lw:Q8KmWzbituyGCkSro#r3, lw:Q8KmWzbituyGCkSro#r4, lw:Q8KmWzbituyGCkSro#r5). Counts: versions.V1.verdicts.supports.studies = 2; versions.V1.verdicts.limits_scope.studies = 2; versions.V1.verdicts.challenges.studies = 0; versions.V1.tested_by_review_class = {preprint: 2, informal: 2}. R2 remains qualified by these methodological differences and qualitative evidence. Neither independent language-model test quantifies 'much of the output'; the original's ~70% restoration at middle layers combines attention compensation with reduced MLP erasure (arXiv:2307.15771#R5). Limits include absence on flat/N-gram training data (arXiv:2603.06592#r2, arXiv:2603.06592#r7) and weak repair in tabular foundation models (lw:NpBufh2z2w4mgHKvm#r1, lw:NpBufh2z2w4mgHKvm#r2, lw:NpBufh2z2w4mgHKvm#r3, lw:NpBufh2z2w4mgHKvm#r4).
suggested_status.open_questions: An independent, quantified test on a language model, ideally a different family, that ablates attention sublayers only (resample or mean) and reports the restored share and the slope by depth, would firm up R2 for the full statement. A failed replication on a language model under the original's recipe would move it toward C. Tests above 10B and on instruct-tuned models would set the level at those scales. Open: is the tabular absence due to model domain, data structure (as arXiv:2603.06592's data dependence suggests) or whole-layer ablation?

source.title: The Hydra Effect: Emergent Self-repair in Language Model Computations
source.authors: Tom McGrath; Matthew Rahtz; János Kramár; Vladimir Mikulik; S. Legg

original_result.setup: The authors resample-ablated attention layers in Chinchilla 7B using Counterfact prompts and measured downstream responses.
original_result.result: Later attention layers partially compensated for ablation. At middle layers, this compensation and less suppression by MLPs together restored approximately 70% of the drop in token logits caused by ablation.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: PCSG-trained and OLMo models showed compensation at early and late training stages.
After attention ablations, llama-3-8b kept the same arithmetic answer as later attention heads became active.
Layerwise compensation was weak in a toy model and absent without hierarchical training data.
Tabular foundation models showed little repair by later layers; robustness mostly reflected components with overlapping functions.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

wording_issues.issue: arXiv:2603.06592 zeroes whole-layer residual contributions and leaves attention-sublayer ablation untested; the checker classifies this method as T2. lw:NpBufh2z2w4mgHKvm resample-ablates whole transformer layers in tabular foundation models. lw:Q8KmWzbituyGCkSro ablates attention heads in llama-3-8b, but its first arithmetic-prompt test removes all heads in layers 10 and 11 together (r1).

The original's approximately 70% restoration at middle layers in Chinchilla 7B under resample ablation on Counterfact prompts combines attention-layer compensation with reduced MLP erasure (R5). In its 17M PCSG-trained model and OLMo-1B experiments, arXiv:2603.06592 zeroes whole-layer residual contributions and measures changes in the immediately following layer's predictive influence, without isolating later attention layers or quantifying restored output. lw:NpBufh2z2w4mgHKvm does not measure later layers' activation changes directly.

In Chinchilla 7B under resample ablation on Counterfact prompts, compensation is incomplete: the slope is below 1 at all layers past layer 13 (R3). About 70% of the logit drop is restored at middle layers, including MLP erasure changes (R5); the illustrative examples are described as largely anecdotal (R1). Under whole-layer resample ablation on binary classification datasets, repaired dataset/layer points are 11% for LimiX-2M, 2% for Mitra, 0% for TabICL-v2 and 2% for TabFM. Mitra and TabFM are partial; TabICL-v2 is absent. These shares do not measure the amount of output restored. arXiv:2603.06592 measures adjacent-layer predictive-influence changes after whole-layer zero ablation, without quantifying restored output. lw:Q8KmWzbituyGCkSro reports qualitative answer preservation in llama-3-8b on an arithmetic prompt (r1, r5).

wording_issues.phrase: ablating one attention layer makes later attention layers compensate
wording_issues.issue: The statement omits conditions. Under whole-layer residual-contribution zero ablation, arXiv:2603.06592 reports no sign of Hydra effect in the flat-DGP toy model (r2), no development in the 17M N-gram-trained model (r7), and a weak layerwise signal in the 6-layer hierarchical-DGP toy (r1). No numerical layerwise value is stated for the flat variant; the near-zero description concerns headwise Hydra, induction and function-vector measures. The study's large-model measure is adjacent-layer predictive-influence change, without a restored-output fraction. Under whole-layer resample ablation in tabular foundation models, Mitra and TabFM each have 2% repaired dataset/layer points (partial, r2 and r4); TabICL-v2 has 0% (absent, r3). The verdicts retain these as limits_scope conditions.

method_sensitivity.what: Layerwise compensation is weak in the hierarchical-DGP toy (r1, does not survive Bonferroni). The flat-DGP toy shows no sign of Hydra effect (r2); no numerical layerwise value is stated, and the near-zero description concerns headwise Hydra, induction and function-vector metrics. Compensation is observed in the 17M PCSG model (r3, r4) and absent in the 17M N-gram model (r7). The text reports compensation as higher in PCSG than in OLMo-1B (r4 note). These experiments zero whole-layer residual contributions; large-model compensation measures only the next layer's predictive-influence change and does not quantify restored output. The study is T2.

method_sensitivity.factor: Layer depth of the ablated layer (original, baseline)
method_sensitivity.what: In Chinchilla 7B under resample ablation on Counterfact prompts, direct and compensatory effects correlate well mainly at intermediate layers. Early layers have large total but little direct effect. The slope is below 1 at every layer past layer 13 (R3). Approximately 70% of the logit drop is restored at middle layers, combining attention compensation with reduced MLP erasure (R5). These aggregate effects do not isolate later-attention compensation: almost all of the layer-23 response occurs in erasure MLPs, so R2 is cannot_determine for V1 and does not establish its restoration fraction.

method_sensitivity.factor: Which layer is ablated (where compensation lands)
method_sensitivity.what: In llama-3-8b on the y=2x+3 ICL prompt, the first patch point carrying the task depends on which layer is ablated. Unablated it is layer 12. Ablating layers 10–11 moves it to before layer 14 (r2). Following layer-13 ablation, the reported patch point shifts from 14 to 16 (r3); retention of the earlier ablations is not explicitly specified.

The repaired share ranges from 0% (TabICL-v2, r3) to 11% (LimiX-2M, r1), and the redundant share from 16% (LimiX-2M) to 78% (TabFM, r4). TabFM has 2% repaired, state partial, and 20% others (r4). CE-versus-DE fits are near zero for LimiX-2M, Mitra and TabFM (r5, r6, r8), while TabICL-v2 shows slope -0.41 with fit 0.58 (r7, cannot_determine per verdict).
In the hierarchical-DGP toy transformer, the layerwise compensation signal is weaker than the headwise signal (r1 verdict reason).
